newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares weighed down by profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares weighed down by profit taking.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.49 percent on Tuesday on a flurry of profit taking by individual investors but market participants forecast prices would bottom out at current levels.
"Many shareholders in newly privatised companies start to sell as soon as they see a slight decline in the share price," said Nina Jarc, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska banka.

But she detected a residual optimism in the market, which climbed strongly in late September and early October, and said prices could resume their advance in November when there more new listings were expected.
The SBI index fell 5.87 points to 1,200.7. Turnover rose to 231.4 million tolars from 229.4 million.
Drug company Lek's issue A had the highest turnover, easing 0.43 percent to 20,600 tolars on volume of 4,647 shares for total turnover of 95.0 million tolars.
Financial consultancy Dadas was the leading decliner, falling 9.95 percent to 17,110 tolars on volume of 633 shares for total turnover of 11.9 million tolars.
Construction company GPG was the top gainer. Its shares rose 10 percent to 7,700 on volume of five shares for total turnover of 0.04 million tolars.
